text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Many decisions in the forestry sector including some investments have been based on too optimistic forest growth forecasts in the 1990s, says Forestry Research Institute.
- Officials who grant asylum should meet applicants, instead of local police which currently do the interviews on which decisions are based, report says. @
- Visa requirements between Finland and Estonia may be lifted at the turn of year, says Interior Minister Jan-Erik Enestam.
- Women's organisations want regular public funding and a similar public status as other interest groups have.
- Occupation influences attitudes on environmental protection more than age, generation or gender.
- Finland cannot unilaterally abandon the use of landmines, says Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen. @

- Reduced third world aid from the industrialised countries comes at a bad time, just when the United Nations is strengthening and past mistakes have taught many good lessons, says UNDP Director James Gustav Speth.
- All nine European Union cultural capitals in 2000 agree on cooperation in Helsinki. The cities are relaxed about sharing the title, hoping to find new forms of lasting European cooperation.
- Big exporters want the markka exchange rate to fall some three to five percent before a possible link to the ERM. @
- Advertisers optimistic on growth, says advertisers' association's annual barometer.

- Finance minister Sauli Niinisto says Finland should have a public sector surplus to make it possible to pursue an own counter-cyclical economic and fiscal policy even in Economic and Monetary Union.
- A majority of Finns -- including motorists -- oppose building more drive-in supermarkets.
